summary: Council adopted the Transportation Master Plan and Active Transportation Plan after directing staff to remove the proposed Hoffman Avenue connection from the future street network. Council gave second and third readings to Bylaws 2253 and 2254 (602 Madrona Place), gave second and third readings and adopted Bylaw 2268 (Form and Character Design Guidelines) and adopted Tree Protection Bylaw No. 2269. Council granted permissive tax exemptions to several non-profit properties and directed staff to amend Bylaw No. 2249 to continue the exemption for 1319 Westhills Drive. Council rescinded a suite of council policies and authorized development actions including issuing DVP26-0005 (1320 Westhills Drive), directing notice for two Temporary Use Permits (890 Goldstream Ave; 4373 West Shore Pkwy), and advancing consideration of rezoning Bylaw 2236 for Massie Drive.

items.title: Permissive Tax Exemption (Special Community Advisory Committee Resolutions - July 7, 2026)
items.matter_title: Permissive tax exemptions for specified properties
items.plain_english_summary: Council granted permissive tax exemptions to several non-profit properties and directed staff to draft necessary bylaws and amend Bylaw No. 2249 for an existing exemption.
items.description: Council granted one-year exemptions to three properties, a ten-year exemption to 550 Goldstream Avenue (M'akola Housing Society), directed staff to amend Bylaw No. 2249 for 1319 Westhills Drive, and directed staff to draft bylaws to enact the exemptions.

motions.motion_text: THAT Council: Grant a one (1) year permissive tax exemption to the following properties: 2775 Spencer Road, Construction Foundation of BC; 202-2800 Bryn Maur Road, Sooke Family Resource Society; 2506 Selwyn Road, Mount Finlayson Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses; and Grant a ten (10) year permissive tax exemption to: 550 Goldstream Avenue, M’akola Housing Society; and Direct staff to amend Bylaw No. 2249 in order to continue the permissive tax exemption provided to 1319 Westhills Drive, Victoria Conservatory of Music; and Direct staff to draft the necessary bylaw(s) to enact the permissive tax exemptions as described in the report dated July 7, 2026.
motions.plain_english_summary: Council approved permissive tax exemptions and directed staff to prepare implementing bylaws and an amendment to Bylaw 2249.

items.title: Application for a Temporary Use Permit at 890 Goldstream Avenue
items.matter_title: Temporary Use Permit - Code Ninjas Westshore (890 Goldstream Avenue)
items.plain_english_summary: Council directed staff to provide notice that it will consider issuing a three-year Temporary Use Permit to Code Ninjas Westshore for 890 Goldstream Avenue, with conditions and non-transferability.
items.description: Council directed staff to provide notice that it will consider issuing a TUP limited to Jesse Bowness doing business as Code Ninjas Westshore for a three-year period and subject to specified terms.

motions.motion_text: THAT Council: Direct staff to provide notice that Council will consider issuing a Temporary Use Permit for a computer programing school for children at 890 Goldstream Avenue, subject to the following terms and conditions: THAT the Temporary Use Permit be issued only to Jesse Bowness, doing business as Code Ninjas Westshore and not to be transferred to any subsequent business or business owner should Code Ninjas Westshore cease to operate; AND THAT the Temporary Use Permit is issued for a period of three years from time of issuance.
motions.plain_english_summary: Council directed staff to provide notice for consideration of a three-year, non-transferable TUP to Code Ninjas Westshore.

items.title: Application for a Temporary Use Permit at 4373 West Shore Parkway
items.matter_title: Temporary Use Permit - 4373 West Shore Parkway (Galaxy RV storage)
items.plain_english_summary: Council directed staff to provide notice that it will consider issuing a Temporary Use Permit to allow vehicle receiving/preparation/storage for 4373 West Shore Parkway, subject to safety and site conditions.
items.description: Council directed staff to provide notice that it will consider issuing a TUP to permit RV receiving/preparation/storage for sale, with conditions including no razor wire, fire extinguisher on site, posted address, and maintained access lane.

motions.motion_text: THAT Council: Direct staff to provide notice that Council will consider issuing a Temporary Use Permit to allow the property at 4373 West Shore Parkway to be used for receiving, preparing, and storage of recreational vehicles for sale at the applicant’s RV Dealership on the adjacent lot (4377 West Shore Parkway) without building a structure that meets the 10% minimum lot coverage, subject to the following terms and conditions: No razor wire fencing; At least 10lb dry chemical fire extinguisher must be available on site at all times; Address for the site to be posted as per City of Langford bylaw; and Maintain an access lane on site for fire suppression for the duration.
motions.plain_english_summary: Council directed staff to provide notice to consider issuing a TUP for RV storage at 4373 West Shore Parkway subject to conditions.

items.title: Elect Respect - Request for Support, Lake Cowichan (Correspondence)
items.plain_english_summary: Council resolved to support the Elect Respect pledge and called on others to support the campaign.
items.description: Council allowed the motion arising and passed a motion committing the City to support the Elect Respect pledge and to call on others to support the campaign and sign the online pledge.

motions.motion_text: THAT the City of Langford Council supports the Elect Respect pledge and commits to: Treat others with respect in all spaces—public, private, and online, Reject and call out harassment, abuse, and personal attacks, Focus debate on ideas and policies, not personal attacks, Help build a supportive culture where people of all backgrounds feel safe to run for and hold office, Call on relevant authorities to ensure the protection of elected officials who face abuse or threats, and Model integrity and respect by holding one another to the highest standards of conduct. AND THAT Council calls on elected officials, organizations and community members to support the Elect Respect campaign and sign the online pledge at www.electrespect.ca.
motions.plain_english_summary: Council endorsed the Elect Respect pledge and encouraged others to sign the pledge.
